remove_sources.reason: CMS identifies MLN2259384 as Rural Emergency Hospitals, not RHC/FQHC distant-site telehealth guidance. The existing transmittal R13776OTN and FQHC/RHC News page remain cited for the telehealth statement.

replacements.before: Immediate priorities for Oklahoma rural hospital leaders: (1) reconcile October RHC telehealth claims now to detect EDI edits, modifier rejections and payment timing changes after CMS required distant-site billing by individual CPT/HCPCS plus telehealth modifiers; (2) verify whether Oklahoma has executed CMS GENEROUS participation terms before changing pharmacy or 340B forecasts; and (3) model state-level Medicaid downside exposure tied to provider-tax funded supplemental payments while tracking final action on proposed rule CMS-2452-P. Separately, Oklahoma RHTP awards are moving from design to subaward execution; require written subaward terms and post-grant sustainability plans. All recommendations are conditional on payer and state documentation and should be implemented as short-cycle operational checks with finance, revenue cycle and Medicaid contacts. Sources: CMS transmittal R13776OTN; CMS MLN guidance; CMS fact sheet CMS-2452-P; CMS GENEROUS press release; Oklahoma RHTP pages;

replacements.before: CMS transmittal R13776OTN and related MLN guidance require RHCs and FQHCs to bill distant-site telehealth by individual CPT/HCPCS service codes plus applicable telehealth modifiers rather than the single G2025 code. CMS pages note the change affects dates of service on/after Oct 1, 2026 while the transmittal lists an Implementation Date of Oct 5, 2026.
replacements.after: CMS transmittal R13776OTN and the CMS FQHC/RHC News page require RHCs and FQHCs to bill distant-site telehealth by individual CPT/HCPCS service codes plus applicable telehealth modifiers rather than the single G2025 code. CMS pages note the change affects dates of service on/after Oct 1, 2026 while the transmittal lists an Implementation Date of Oct 5, 2026.

replacements.before: I recommend three prioritized actions with owners, gates and short-cycle deliverables. Action one: reconcile RHC distant-site telehealth production claims for dates of service October 1 onward by extracting a representative sample through the internal checkpoint date, confirming CPT and HCPCS code selection and telehealth modifier usage, reconciling remittances and logging payer-specific rejections for corrective edits. Assign revenue cycle, RHC operations and IT and set the internal editorial checkpoint on October 21. Action two: request written OHCA confirmation of GENEROUS participation execution and obtain any state implementation terms including covered product lists, MCO passthrough instructions and pharmacy or 340B operational guidance before changing forecasts or contracts. Assign Medicaid, pharmacy and finance teams and retain the correspondence for audit. Action three: assemble finance, Medicaid managed-care and CFO teams to model state-level Medicaid downside that isolates provider-tax funded supplemental-payment exposure and produces cash-stress scenarios under CMS-2452-P assumptions, engaging legal and requesting state budget or OHCA documentation. Each action needs an owner, a deliverable date or checkpoint and a decision gate that prevents budget rebasing absent written state or payer documentation.
replacements.after: I recommend three prioritized actions with owners, gates and short-cycle deliverables. Assign Medicaid, pharmacy and finance teams and retain the correspondence for audit. Action three: assemble finance, Medicaid managed-care and CFO teams to model state-level Medicaid downside that isolates provider-tax funded supplemental-payment exposure and produces cash-stress scenarios under CMS-2452-P assumptions, engaging legal and requesting state budget or OHCA documentation. Each action needs an owner, a deliverable date or checkpoint and a decision gate that prevents budget rebasing absent written state or payer documentation.

replacements.before: Two internal editorial checkpoints enforce short-cycle discipline and collaborative decision making. First, complete an internal reconciliation checkpoint by October 21 for a representative sample of October telehealth claims, confirm telehealth modifier usage and document payer-specific rejections; if widespread payer rejections are identified escalate to remediation. Second, complete a preparation checkpoint by October 23 to produce RHTP post-grant sustainability materials for upcoming state collaborative meetings, including project problem statements, participating communities, staffing, maintenance assumptions and estimated recurring costs; if subaward terms fail to specify sustainability negotiate phased disbursements or decline unfunded recurring commitments. Use these checkpoints as decision gates that trigger remediation, negotiation or board notification as appropriate.
replacements.after: Two internal planning actions support short-cycle review and collaborative decision making. First, the previously suggested October 21 reconciliation checkpoint has passed. Agree a new internal review date for a representative sample of October telehealth claims, confirm modifier usage and document payer-specific rejections; if widespread payer rejections are identified, escalate to remediation. No replacement due date is assigned in this edition. Second, use October 23 as a suggested internal preparation checkpoint for RHTP sustainability materials, including project problem statements, participating communities, staffing, maintenance assumptions and estimated recurring costs. This is not a federal deadline. Verify applicable subaward terms before committing recurring expenditure, and use the review to identify remediation, negotiation or board questions rather than assume grant conditions.
